results.content:
As the U.S. races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027.
10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RoboStore, a leading distributor of foreign humanoid and quadruped robots in North America, today announced the public launch of Robo Inc., a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems integration company built to help organizations deploy practical robotic solutions in America. As the U.S. races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027.
The company combines global robotics platforms and components with U.S.-based engineering, software, integration, security and safety testing, production, service and support. Its planned 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, is expected to begin producing U.S.-localized robotic solutions in January 2027.
The company will solve the most common customer need: a robotic solution that can be deployed against specific operational problems today, with realistic performance expectations, clear safety boundaries and a plan for integration into existing workflows – not an all-in-one humanoid promised to handle every task.
Robo Inc. draws on patterns seen across thousands of purchases, deployments, repairs and integration requests from customers including Harvard, MIT, Amazon, and Nvidia.

results.content:
### [**RoboStore to Advance U.S. Localization of Robotics with Launch of Robo Inc.**]()  
**RoboStore to Advance U.S. Localization of Robotics with Launch of Robo Inc.**  
*After a Year in Stealth, Leading Robotics Distributor Unveils New York-Based Manufacturing & Systems Integration Company*  
RoboStore, a leading distributor of foreign humanoid and quadruped robots in North America, today announced the public launch of Robo Inc., a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems integration company built to help organizations deploy practical robotic solutions in America. As the U.S. races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027.  
Based on real-world learnings from RoboStore selling and deploying more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots while serving 4,500 customers, Robo Inc. will build America's robotics infrastructure with an ecosystem that combines global robotics supply chains with U.S.-based engineering, software, integration, production, testing, service and support. Importantly, the company is designing security and safety checkpoints into its integration process, including reviews of data flows, network access, software controls, operating environments and application-specific risks.
Robo Inc. draws on patterns seen across thousands of purchases, deployments, repairs and integration requests from customers including Harvard, MIT, Amazon, and Nvidia. The company will solve the most common customer need: a robotic solution that can be deployed against specific operational problems today, with realistic performance expectations, clear safety boundaries and a plan for integration into existing workflows - not an all-in-one humanoid promised to handle every task.  
"With U.S.-based assembly, localized data infrastructure, and domestic integration, Robo Inc. will create a robotics platform built for American compliance," said Teddy Haggerty, Founder and CEO of RoboStore and Robo Inc. "RoboStore gave us a front-row seat to what customers actually need from robotics. Rather than more far-out promises, customers want solutions that can be deployed now, built around a specific job and supported over time. We're moving beyond selling robots to building a localized ecosystem that allows U.S. organizations to put robotics to work responsibly and at scale."  
Robo Inc. is hardware-agnostic and will select robotic platforms and components based on the requirements of each application. The new company will work with customers to address applicable cybersecurity, safety and regulatory requirements without overstating what current robotic systems can do.
RoboStore will continue supporting its installed base and current inventory, including parts, repairs and upgrades for the platforms it services. Roboverse, the company's 4000+ member robotics developer community, will continue to operate under the Robo Inc. umbrella.  
About Robo Inc.  
Robo Inc. is a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems integration company building deployable, application-specific solutions through a global-to-local operating model. The company combines global robotics platforms and components with U.S.-based engineering, software, integration, security and safety testing, production, service and support. Its planned 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, is expected to begin producing U.S.-localized robotic solutions in January 2027.  
Learn more at RoboInc.com

results.name: Facing Ban, US Seller of Chinese Robots Makes Domestic Manufacturing Push
results.content:
RoboStore, a major distributor of Chinese-made robots, is pushing to manufacture its systems domestically following the [US ban on foreign-made advanced robots](https://au.pcmag.com/topic-2/119036/the-fccs-next-target-foreign-made-humanoid-robots-and-power-inverters).  
New York-based RoboStore has been selling humanoid and dog-like robots from Chinese vendor Unitree. But on Monday, it launched Robo Incorporated, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company.  
“As the US races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027,” the company said.  
Although humanoid robots are an emerging market, you may have seen them on social media, at trade shows, or at company events. RoboStore notes that it’s sold and deployed “more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots while serving 4,500 customers,” including Nvidia, Amazon, and Harvard University.  
The company’s website sells a whole catalog of Unitree models, ranging from $10,000 to $20,000 to higher-end machines costing over $100,000. The whole business now faces an uncertain future after the White House decided to ban foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots, along with [robot vacuums](https://au.pcmag.com/robot-vacuums/119054/fcc-ban-on-foreign-made-robots-includes-robot-vacuums), over concerns they could be hijacked for spying or sabotage.
US robot companies, including Boston Dynamics, Tesla, Figure, and Agility Robotics, stand to benefit from the ban. Now RoboStore is trying to build up its own domestic manufacturing base, which promises to combine global robotics supply chains with US-based engineering, software, integration, production, testing, service, and support.  
“Importantly, the company is designing security and safety checkpoints into its integration process, including reviews of data flows, network access, software controls, operating environments, and application-specific risks,” the company says. “Robo Inc. draws on patterns seen across thousands of purchases, deployments, repairs, and integration requests from customers.”  
However, the newly launched Robo Inc. has more modest ambitions than other players seeking to build general-purpose humanoid robots that can serve as artificial butlers or factory workers. It's focused on “the most common customer need: a robotic solution that can be deployed against specific operational problems today, with realistic performance expectations, clear safety boundaries, and a plan for integration into existing workflows —not an all-in-one humanoid promised to handle every task.”

results.name: Robo Inc. Launches US Humanoid Robot Integrator; China Spy Law Still Follows Hardware
results.content:
RoboStore, North America's most active distributor of humanoid and quadruped robots, today publicly launched **Robo Inc.**, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company designed to fill the compliance gap left by the Federal Communications Commission's [July 28 decision](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-423682A1.pdf) to block new Chinese-made advanced robots from the American market. The company says it will open a 66,000-square-foot (roughly 6,130 square meters) facility on Long Island, New York, expected to be operational by January 2027 — a concrete deadline and a named address in a sector that has historically offered neither.  
The launch arrives at a moment when the American robotics market is genuinely stuck. Chinese manufacturers currently account for approximately 51 percent of global humanoid robot production, with companies like Unitree offering fully operational humanoids starting at $13,500 — a price that domestic American manufacturers cannot match. Agility Robotics' Digit, the most commercially deployed US-made humanoid robot, operates under a Robots-as-a-Service model [priced at approximately $8,500 per month](https://blog.robozaps.com/b/agility-robotics-digit-review) per unit, with outright purchase equivalent that has historically exceeded $250,000. That price gap is the market reality Robo Inc. is attempting to exploit.
### What Comes Next  
The 66,000-square-foot (6,130 square meters) Long Island facility is planned to begin producing US-localized robotic solutions in January 2027. Between now and then, Robo Inc. will need to hire domestic engineering talent, establish supplier relationships, secure necessary certifications, and demonstrate to prospective customers that its security review process is rigorous enough to satisfy both corporate IT teams and, for those customers who need it, regulatory requirements.  
The company's existing RoboStore customer base — 4,500 organizations with more than 1,500 robots already deployed — gives it a starting market that few new entrants could claim. The developer community it has built through Roboverse gives it a software ecosystem to draw on. What it does not yet have is a clear answer to the question that every enterprise security team will ask: under what specific compliance framework does a Robo Inc.-integrated robot qualify as US-compliant, and what documentation will the company provide to certify that standard has been met?  
When Robo Inc. can answer that question with a named framework, a named certifying body, and a named set of documentation deliverables, the gap between its stated ambitions and its operational reality will be measurable. Until then, it is asking American enterprises to trust that the integration layer is enough — a reasonable ask for some buyers, and an insufficient one for others.
## Frequently Asked Questions  
### What does Robo Inc. actually do that RoboStore does not?  
RoboStore distributes foreign-made robots — including Unitree platforms — to American customers. Robo Inc. adds US-based assembly, software integration, security hardening, and testing to that supply chain, creating a "global-to-local" model in which the hardware may still come from foreign (including Chinese) manufacturers, but the integration work — security review of data flows, network access, software controls, and application-specific risks — happens on US soil under American engineering oversight. The planned Long Island facility will be the physical location where that integration work occurs, beginning in January 2027.

results.name: RoboStore Launches U.S. Robotics Manufacturing and Integration Company Named Robo Inc.
results.content:
**Insider Brief**  
- RoboStore has launched Robo Inc., a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems-integration company, with plans to open a 66,000-square-foot Long Island facility by the first quarter of 2027.
- The launch comes shortly after new U.S. restrictions on advanced foreign-made robots, while Robo Inc. plans to emphasize U.S.-based assembly, localized data infrastructure, security reviews and application-specific integration.
- Robo Inc. will take a hardware-agnostic approach built on RoboStore’s experience selling and deploying more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots to about 4,500 customers, including Harvard, MIT, Amazon and Nvidia.  
After a year in stealth, foreign-made robot distributor RoboStore has launched a U.S.-based [robotics](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22robotics%22) manufacturing and systems-integration company called [Robo Inc](https://www.roboinc.com/).  
[According to Robo Inc.](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/robostore-to-advance-us-localization-of-robotics-with-launch-of-robo-inc-302847020.html), the New York-based company plans to open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island that is expected to be fully operational by the first quarter of 2027. The company said the site will support engineering, software, integration, production, testing, service and customer support.
The public launch comes just two weeks after [the U.S. banned new advanced foreign-made robotics](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/07/29/trump-administration-bans-new-chinese-humanoids-other-foreign-made-robotics-power-inverters/).  
“With U.S.-based assembly, localized data infrastructure, and domestic integration, Robo Inc. will create a robotics platform built for American compliance,” said Teddy Haggerty, founder and CEO of RoboStore and Robo Inc. “RoboStore gave us a front-row seat to what customers actually need from robotics. Rather than more far-out promises, customers want solutions that can be deployed now, built around a specific job and supported over time. We’re moving beyond selling robots to building a localized ecosystem that allows U.S. organizations to put robotics to work responsibly and at scale.”  
The company noted that the new business builds on RoboStore’s experience distributing foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in North America. RoboStore said it has sold and deployed more than 1,500 robots and served about 4,500 customers, including [Harvard](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22Harvard%22), [MIT](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22MIT%22), [Amazon](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22Amazon%22) and [Nvidia](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22Nvidia%22). RoboStore is also an official distributor of China’s [Unitree Robotics](https://theaiinsider.tech/?s=%22Unitree%22), in the news this week for its Shanghai IPO.
Rather than developing a single general-purpose robot, Robo Inc. will take a hardware-agnostic approach, selecting robot platforms and components based on the needs of individual applications. The company said it will focus on systems that can address defined operational problems with clear expectations for performance, safety and integration into existing workflows.  
The approach is based in part on patterns RoboStore said it has seen across purchases, deployments, repairs and integration requests. The company said customers often need help turning available robot hardware into systems that can perform practical work, rather than waiting for fully general humanoid robots capable of handling a wide range of tasks.  
Robo Inc. is also incorporating security and safety reviews into its integration process and those checks will cover areas including data flows, network access, software controls, operating environments and risks tied to specific applications, according to the company.  
Robo Inc. said it will also work with customers on applicable cybersecurity, safety and regulatory requirements as part of deployment planning.  
RoboStore added that it will continue to support its existing installed base and inventory, including parts, repairs and upgrades for the robot platforms it services. Roboverse, its developer community of more than 4,000 members, will continue operating under the Robo Inc. umbrella.
